# Assayance — 试真法 · Falsifiable Assurance

> A discipline for assaying the instruments of assurance before trusting them.
> Coined term in the LGD (Lifecycle Governance Doctrine) theory stack.
> Cite as: Zhao, S. (2026). Assayance: Falsifiable Assurance. SynomosAI.

## The claim

A check that has never been observed failing has not been shown to be capable of
failing; therefore it is not yet a check. A gate that cannot fail, a test that
cannot go red, a policy that defaults to allow, an evidence artifact nobody
recomputes, a document describing a safeguard the code does not contain — these
read as assurance while producing none.

## Five tests, applicable to any assurance artifact

- **T1 · Negative control** — break the protected thing; the check must fail.
  Restore; it must pass. A check never seen failing is not a check.
- **T2 · Absence must reach the exit code** — if a required input is missing, the
  process must exit non-zero. A missing input recorded as a log line, a neutral
  marker, or a skip never fails, so the gate is blind where it matters most.
- **T3 · The criterion is itself under test** — ask whether the criterion would
  also pass when nothing was satisfied. "Non-empty" and ">0 results" are not
  quality bars.
- **T4 · A description is a claim** — a comment, docstring or policy asserting
  behaviour must be tested or deleted. There is no third option.
- **T5 · A proxy is not an identity judgment** — name the metric, the decision it
  stands for, and a case where they disagree. Also: a value displayed anywhere
  needs its own route to verification, because a correct artifact can sit beside
  a wrong number and the number is what gets read.

## Precursor (T0): prior art before invention

- R1: write queries like repository names — `gh search repos` matches name,
  description and topics, and does not index READMEs.
- R2: sort by stars, then read the last-commit date anyway; a popularity proxy
  is not an identity judgment, and star-farm aggregators rank first.
- R3: use a ladder of queries and record which rung hit; accepting the first
  non-empty result is how a stale one-star script gets filed as "existing
  solutions", which is worse than a blank.

## Falsifiability conditions

T1's necessity is bounded if equivalent results are demonstrable without ever
observing a control fail. The domain is narrower than claimed if the dominant
cost of failure is crashes rather than silent passes. The discipline degrades to
advice if the five tests cannot be mechanised.

## Boundary

Not a standard, no conformance claim, no priority claim. Every ingredient is
public (Popper's falsifiability, laboratory controls, mutation testing,
metrology's instrument verification, policy-as-code default-deny). What is named
here is their convergence into one discipline applied to assurance claims
themselves. No results are promised.

## Where the evidence lives

The doctrine is this repository. The catalogue — fourteen documented silent
failure modes with reproductions, self-checks and runnable detectors, plus
twelve recorded defects found by these methods — is:
https://github.com/zhaoxinghua09-cell/silent-failure-catalog
